logp.method_description: The partition coefficients (log P) of the complexes in n-octanol:water were obtained, using the shake flask method according to OECD guidelines5. First, a saturated solution of water and n-octanol was prepared by stirring the two solvents together for 24 hours and separating the phases after that. Stock compound solutions (0.1 mmol∙L-1 in 1% DMSO) were dissolved in 25 mL of saturated water. The samples were prepared by mixing 7.5 mL of stock solution with 7.5 mL of saturated n-octanol and mixed in an orbital agitator at 1000 rpm for 2 h. Then, samples were centrifuged at 4200 rpm for 15 min. The aqueous phases (7.0 mL) were subjected to 1:1 (V/V) aqua regia treatment and heated until complete drying. The residue was calcined at 600 ºC for 20 min. The solids were dissolved with an aqueous solution of aqua regia 1% and the gold content in each replicate was quantified by ICP-OES. The concentration was calibrated with standard gold solution for ICP in HCl 1g L-1 (Supelco®).The partition coefficients (log P) were calculated using concentration data from both phases (Eq. 1), considering the concentration in octanol is the difference from stock solution and the concentration measured in water. The experiments were performed in duplicate. log P = log([Au]octanol / [Au]water)
